headings.title: Exclusive original jurisdiction of juvenile and family courts
headings.reviewNote: Vests exclusive original jurisdiction in juvenile or family courts over care and treatment, status, law/ordinance violations (with traffic, curfew, and tobacco exceptions), adoptions, DSS guardianship, under-18 protection orders, and child sex-trafficking victims; source note notes section 195.130 was transferred to section 579.105 effective 1-01-17.

headings.title: Transfer of proceedings, jurisdiction, or supervision and change of judge
headings.reviewNote: Governs discretionary transfers of matters, proceedings, jurisdiction, and supervision to the child's county of residence or offense county, mandatory one change of judge upon motion, and transmittal of certified legal and social records.

headings.title: Seventy-two-hour notice to county of child's residence upon custody
headings.reviewNote: Requires notifying the juvenile court of the child's county of residence within seventy-two hours when a child is taken into custody in another county.

headings.title: Home school or FPE school attendance verification and reporting
headings.reviewNote: Requires a juvenile officer investigating a sole alleged section 167.031 violation involving a home school or FPE school to contact a parent to verify instruction before reporting, and requires any report to go to the prosecuting attorney of the child's county of residence.

headings.title: Parental disability or disease not basis for removal without causal harm
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits using a parent's disability or disease as a basis for a need-of-care determination or custody removal without a specific showing of a causal relation between the disability or disease and harm to the child.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 editorial headings for 211.031 governing exclusive original jurisdiction, transfers, 72-hour custody notice, home/FPE school attendance reports, and parental disability limits.

headings.title: Written notice of right to protective custody hearing
headings.reviewNote: Requires the juvenile or family court, except in supreme court pilot project circuits, to notify parties in writing of the right to a protective custody hearing when a child is taken into custody under section 211.031(1)(1).

headings.title: Protective custody hearing within three days upon request
headings.reviewNote: Requires holding a protective custody hearing within three days of any party's request, excluding weekends and legal holidays, and requires status conference notice in supreme court pilot circuits.

headings.title: Mandatory three-day court proceeding and supreme court rules
headings.reviewNote: Directs the Missouri supreme court by February 1, 2005, to require a mandatory court proceeding within three business days in all section 211.031(1)(1) cases and promulgate implementing rules, while allowing expansion of pilot projects.

headings.title: Adjudication, dispositional, and periodic review hearing timelines
headings.reviewNote: Requires an adjudication hearing within sixty days with written notice, a dispositional hearing within ninety days if sufficient cause exists, and review hearings every ninety to one hundred twenty days in the first year and at least every six months thereafter.

headings.title: Evidence relevant to necessity of detaining child out of custody
headings.reviewNote: Permits the court at all hearings under this section to receive testimony and other evidence relevant to the necessity of detaining the child out of the custody of parents, guardian, or custodian.

headings.title: Supreme court rules on effect of untimely hearings
headings.reviewNote: Requires the Missouri supreme court by January 1, 2005, to develop rules regarding the effect of untimely hearings.

headings.title: School record forwarding or continuation at same school after removal
headings.reviewNote: Requires automatic forwarding of school records upon children's division notification within two business days, or permitting the child to continue attending the same school upon request whenever possible, with procedures established by the division and DESE.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 7 editorial headings for 211.032 governing abuse and neglect protective custody hearings, supreme court rules, hearing timelines, evidence, and school record transfers.

headings.title: Prohibition on detaining persons under eighteen in adult jail
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits detaining any person under age eighteen in a jail or other adult detention facility as defined in section 211.151, except those transferred to a court of general jurisdiction under section 211.071.

headings.title: No civil or criminal liability for good-faith belief on jurisdiction
headings.reviewNote: Provides that this section creates no civil or criminal liability for law enforcement, juvenile officers, school personnel, or court personnel for actions or omissions based on a good-faith belief a minor is not under juvenile court jurisdiction.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 editorial headings for 211.033 governing prohibition on adult jail detention for persons under eighteen and good-faith immunity from liability.

headings.title: Petition by parent or custodian to extend jurisdiction until age eighteen
headings.reviewNote: Permits a parent, legal guardian, or legal custodian to petition the circuit court of residence, between the minor child's fifteenth and eighteenth birthdays, to extend juvenile court jurisdiction until age eighteen.

headings.title: Proof of service, nonparent affidavits, and appointed counsel for minor
headings.reviewNote: Requires verified proof of service, certified custody documents, and natural-parent consent or unavailability affidavits from nonparent petitioners, and requires the court to appoint an attorney for the minor paid by the petitioner.

headings.title: Order extending jurisdiction until age eighteen and certified-adult exception
headings.reviewNote: Requires an order keeping the minor under juvenile court jurisdiction until age eighteen and subject to compulsory school attendance under section 167.031, except that a certified adult remains a certified adult for criminal law and procedure.

headings.title: No civil or criminal liability for good-faith belief on jurisdiction
headings.reviewNote: Provides that this section creates no civil or criminal liability for law enforcement, juvenile officers, school personnel, or court personnel for actions or omissions based on a good-faith belief a minor is not under juvenile court jurisdiction.

headings.title: Expiration tied to effective date of section 211.021(1) amendments
headings.reviewNote: Provides that this section expires when amendments to section 211.021(1) take effect under section 211.021(2); archived Revisor's Note states S.B. 793 merged with S.B. 800 (2018) repealed section 211.021(2) effective 1-01-21.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 editorial headings for 211.034 governing petitions to extend juvenile court jurisdiction until age eighteen, affidavits and appointed counsel, extension orders, good-faith immunity, and expiration (Revisor's Note notes section 211.021(2) was repealed effective 1-01-21).

headings.title: Petition, best-interest factors, and bars to returning youth to custody
headings.reviewNote: Permits the juvenile officer, children's division, or youth under twenty-one to petition to return custody until age twenty-one, sets venue and mandatory best-interest factors, and bars return of youth committed to another agency, under guardianship, or with a felony guilty plea or finding.

headings.title: Youth duty to cooperate with children's division case plan
headings.reviewNote: Requires the youth to cooperate with the case plan developed for the youth by the children's division in consultation with the youth.

headings.title: Definition of youth eligible for return to children's division custody
headings.reviewNote: Defines youth as a person age eighteen or older and under twenty-one who was in children's division foster care custody at any time in the two years preceding the eighteenth birthday.

headings.title: Discretionary termination of care and supervision before age twenty-one
headings.reviewNote: Permits the court, on motion of the children's division or youth, to terminate care and supervision before age twenty-one if services are unavailable, no longer needed, or the youth declines to cooperate with the case plan.

headings.title: Youth discretionary request for guardian ad litem appointment
headings.reviewNote: Permits the youth, at the youth's discretion, to request appointment of a guardian ad litem, who shall serve under section 210.160 if appointed.

headings.title: Mandatory review hearings at least once every six months
headings.reviewNote: Requires the court to hold review hearings as necessary, but in no event less than once every six months while the youth remains in children's division custody.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 editorial headings for 211.036 governing petitions to return released youth to children's division custody, case plan cooperation, youth definition, early termination, guardian ad litem requests, and six-month review hearings.

headings.title: Prompt return of child to qualifying nonoffending parent and presumption
headings.reviewNote: Requires prompt return of a child to a nonoffending parent entitled to physical custody when five statutory conditions are met, and creates a rebuttable presumption against specified criminal or abuse/neglect conduct absent a finding of actual harm or endangerment.

headings.title: Preserved discretion of division or court to return child to any individual
headings.reviewNote: Provides that nothing in this section prevents the division or the court from exercising discretion to return a child or children to the custody of any individual.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 editorial headings for 211.037 governing prompt return of custody to a qualifying nonoffending parent and preserved discretion to return a child to any individual.

headings.title: Prohibition on reuniting or placing child in home with specified offenders
headings.reviewNote: Bars reuniting a child with a parent or placing a child in a home where the parent or any resident was found guilty of enumerated chapter 566, 568, or 573 offenses (including prior versions) when a child was the victim.

headings.title: Court discretion for other chapter 566 or 568 and out-of-state offenses
headings.reviewNote: Permits the juvenile court to exercise discretion regarding placement in a home where a parent or resident was found guilty of or pled guilty to unlisted chapter 566 or 568 offenses or equivalent out-of-state child-victim offenses.

headings.title: One-thousand-foot residence ban for child who abused another child
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits a child determined by the juvenile court to have abused another child from residing within one thousand feet of the abused child's residence, child care facility, or school until the abused child turns eighteen, except for siblings or children living in the same home.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 editorial headings for 211.038 governing mandatory placement bars for specified child-victim offenses, court discretion for other chapter 566/568 offenses, and 1,000-foot residence restrictions for abusing children.

headings.title: Oral and written rights advisement prior to questioning in offense cases
headings.reviewNote: Requires advising a child orally and in writing prior to questioning when taken into custody under section 211.031(1)(2) or (3) of the six enumerated rights, including silence, custodian presence, counsel, stopping questioning, and potential adult-transfer use.

headings.title: Duty of juvenile officer to halt questioning upon child's notice
headings.reviewNote: Requires the juvenile officer to halt or discontinue any questioning by law enforcement upon notice from the child that the child wishes to stop being questioned.

headings.title: Advisement of juvenile officer's limited, non-advocate role
headings.reviewNote: Requires the juvenile officer to ensure the child is advised of the juvenile officer's limited role and specifically that the juvenile officer is not legal counsel or an advocate for the child during law enforcement questioning.

headings.title: Prohibition on juvenile officer participating in law enforcement questioning
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits the juvenile officer from participating in law enforcement questioning by asking questions or soliciting information from the child regarding the alleged offense or offenses.

headings.title: Questioning limits and recording admissibility in abuse and neglect custody
headings.reviewNote: Governs halting questioning on abuse/neglect allegations in section 211.031(1)(1) custody cases (preserving care/placement questions), establishes presumptive admissibility of pre-adjudication state recordings unless shown unreliable by clear and convincing evidence, and excludes section 491.075 or 492.304 criminal statements.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 editorial headings for 211.059 governing juvenile Miranda warnings, halting questioning, juvenile officer role limits, and questioning/recording rules in abuse and neglect custody cases.

headings.title: Immediate delivery of arrested child to juvenile officer or court
headings.reviewNote: Requires immediate and direct delivery of a child taken into custody for an offense, with information and personal property, to the juvenile court, juvenile officer, or person acting for the child.

headings.title: Duty of non-juvenile judge to transfer minor case to juvenile court
headings.reviewNote: Requires a non-juvenile circuit, associate circuit, or municipal judge to forthwith transfer or refer the case and direct delivery of the person, information, and property to juvenile court upon ascertaining age under eighteen at the alleged offense or juvenile court jurisdiction.

headings.title: Examination of detention reasons and immediate release or continuation
headings.reviewNote: Requires the juvenile court, upon learning a child is in detention, to examine the reasons and immediately order release or continued detention pending a hearing upon a filed petition or motion to modify and probable cause under section 211.031(1)(2) or (3).

headings.title: Twenty-four-hour detention limit, three-day hearing, and notice
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits detention over twenty-four hours without a court-ordered detention hearing, requires release if the hearing is not held within three business days absent good-cause continuance, and requires expeditious notice of hearing and right to counsel.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 editorial headings for 211.061 governing delivery of arrested children to juvenile court, transfers from non-juvenile judges, detention review, and detention hearing timelines.

headings.title: Twenty-four-hour secure detention limit for status offense violations
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits holding a child accused under section 211.031(1)(2) in secure detention over twenty-four hours (excluding weekends and legal holidays) absent a probable cause hearing finding a valid court order violation and one of three specified records.

headings.title: Statutory definitions of secure detention and valid court order
headings.reviewNote: Defines secure detention and valid court order for purposes of this section.

headings.title: Inapplicability to section 211.031(1)(3) jurisdiction, adjudication, or charges
headings.reviewNote: Exempts children taken under jurisdiction, adjudicated, or currently charged under subdivision (3) of subsection 1 of section 211.031 from this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 editorial headings for 211.063 governing twenty-four-hour secure detention limits for status offenders, definitions, and non-applicability to section 211.031(1)(3) cases.

headings.title: Discretionary and mandatory certification hearings and moving party duties
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes discretionary transfer hearings for specified offenses (ages 14-18), mandates hearings for enumerated serious offenses or prior felonies (ages 12-18), assigns duties to the moving party, and sets fourteen-day prosecutor notification and motion deadlines.

headings.title: Automatic adult jurisdiction over post-eighteen offenses of retained wards
headings.reviewNote: Automatically terminates continuing juvenile court jurisdiction over a new criminal offense allegedly committed by a person between ages eighteen and twenty-one upon apprehension and arrest, placing the offense in a court of general jurisdiction under section 211.041.

headings.title: Effect of willful misrepresentation of age on criminal proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Provides that knowing and willful age misrepresentation by a juvenile does not affect resulting actions or proceedings and allows evidence obtained during the misrepresentation to be used under adult evidentiary rules.

headings.title: Written notification of certification hearing to child and custodian
headings.reviewNote: Requires written notification of a transfer hearing to the juvenile and custodian as provided in sections 211.101 and 211.111, permits waiver of notice by the custodian, and specifies required statements of hearing purpose.

headings.title: Consultation between juvenile officer and prosecuting attorney on charges
headings.reviewNote: Requires juvenile officer consultation with the prosecuting or circuit attorney, sharing of reports, JDTA form, and prior adjudication dispositions, bars pre-determination disclosure, and makes JDTA recommendations non-mandatory guidelines.

headings.title: Mandatory consideration of legally sufficient charges in detention assessment
headings.reviewNote: Requires the juvenile officer in every incident to consider legally sufficient charges submitted by law enforcement on the JDTA form, provide the completed form to law enforcement, and defines legally sufficient.

headings.title: Fingerprinting, central repository reporting, MULES access, and closure
headings.reviewNote: Requires law enforcement to collect fingerprints and forward detention information where fingerprinting is required, requires juvenile officers and courts to report adjudication/delinquency/custody data to the central repository for MULES criminal justice access, and closes records under section 610.120.

headings.title: Written social investigation report and statutory certification criteria
headings.reviewNote: Requires a written report developing all available information on ten enumerated criteria (including racial disparity in certification) for determining whether the child is a proper subject for the juvenile justice system.

headings.title: Contents and required findings of dismissal and transfer order
headings.reviewNote: Requires a dismissal order transferring a child for adult prosecution to contain findings on jurisdiction, representation by counsel, presence of child and counsel at the hearing, and reasons underlying the transfer decision.

headings.title: Delivery of dismissal order and petition to prosecuting attorney
headings.reviewNote: Requires sending a copy of the petition or motion to modify and the order of dismissal to the prosecuting attorney.

headings.title: Termination of juvenile court jurisdiction upon adult conviction
headings.reviewNote: Forever terminates juvenile court jurisdiction over a transferred child for state law or municipal ordinance violations upon adult conviction, except as provided in subsection 12.

headings.title: Juvenile jurisdiction over later offenses after adult acquittal
headings.reviewNote: Provides that if a transferred child is found not guilty by a court of general jurisdiction, the juvenile court shall have jurisdiction over any later misdemeanor or felony offense, subject to certification under this section.

headings.title: Setting of adjudicatory hearing date upon denial of certification motion
headings.reviewNote: Requires the court to set a date for the hearing on the petition under section 211.171 if it does not dismiss the petition or motion to modify for adult prosecution.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 13 editorial headings for 211.071 governing adult certification motions, mandatory hearings, age misrepresentation, JDTA consultation, fingerprinting, criteria, dismissal orders, and jurisdictional effects (Revisor's Note notes H.B. 2637 & 3155 repealed S.B. 888's 2026 version effective 8-28-26).

headings.title: Continued juvenile detention and motion to transfer to adult jail
headings.reviewNote: Keeps a pretrial-certified juvenile under eighteen in secure juvenile detention pending appeal and adult charges unless bond is posted or transferred, permits the juvenile officer to move for adult-jail transfer, and lists parties entitled to be present and present evidence.

headings.title: Court determination and best interest of justice placement standard
headings.reviewNote: Requires continued secure juvenile detention unless the court makes findings that adult jail placement is in the best interest of justice after weighing eight enumerated factors.

headings.title: Mandatory thirty-day review hearings for juveniles held in adult jail
headings.reviewNote: Requires a review hearing once every thirty days while a certified juvenile is held in adult jail, and directs return to adult jail if released and subsequently detained on a release or bond violation.

headings.title: One-hundred-eighty-day maximum limit on adult jail pretrial detention
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits holding a certified juvenile in adult jail over one hundred eighty days absent good-cause extension or waiver through counsel, requires transfer back to secure juvenile detention if unextended, and requires thirty-day hearings during any extension.

headings.title: Transfer of previously certified juveniles from adult jail to juvenile facility
headings.reviewNote: Required transfer effective December 31, 2021, of previously pretrial-certified juveniles under eighteen certified before August 28, 2021, from adult jail to secure juvenile detention absent a best-interest-of-justice finding under subsection 2.

headings.title: Application of federal Prison Rape Elimination Act protections in adult jails
headings.reviewNote: Requires pretrial-certified juveniles under eighteen held in adult jails under the best-interest-of-justice exception to remain subject to PREA protections and be physically separated from adult inmates.

headings.title: Motion to reconsider detention placement of certified juvenile
headings.reviewNote: Permits the juvenile officer to file a motion to reconsider placement if the certified juvenile remains in juvenile detention, with subsection 2 factors and subsection 1 hearing rights, allowing amendment if juvenile detention is not in the best interest of justice.

headings.title: Bail and bond hearings conducted in adult criminal proceeding
headings.reviewNote: Requires bond setting, posting, and bond forfeiture proceedings to be held in the pretrial-certified juvenile's adult criminal case.

headings.title: Transfer to adult facility upon age eighteen, guilty plea, or conviction
headings.reviewNote: Requires transferring the juvenile from juvenile detention to the appropriate adult facility upon attaining age eighteen or upon a plea of guilty or conviction on the adult charges.

headings.title: County jail staff responsibility for transport and contracted services
headings.reviewNote: Assigns responsibility for transportation and contracted services for a certified juvenile remaining in secure juvenile detention to county jail staff as in other adult custody criminal cases.

headings.title: County jail liaison for pretrial-certified juvenile in detention
headings.reviewNote: Requires county jail staff to designate a liaison for each pretrial-certified juvenile in juvenile detention to assist communication on visitation, legal case status, medical and mental health needs, and phone contact.

headings.title: Application of section 211.156 per diem provisions
headings.reviewNote: Applies the per diem provisions of section 211.156 to certified juveniles held in a secure juvenile detention facility.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 12 editorial headings for 211.072 governing continued secure juvenile detention for pretrial-certified juveniles, adult-jail transfer hearings, 30-day reviews, 180-day cap, PREA separation, county jail transport/liaison duties, and per diem.

headings.title: Dual jurisdiction blended sentencing authority of circuit court
headings.reviewNote: Requires the court to consider dual jurisdiction for certified offenders under eighteen upon conviction or guilty plea, authorizes a juvenile disposition with suspended adult sentence and DYS custody upon DYS agreement and space availability, and requires on-the-record findings if DYS agrees but is not used.

headings.title: Hearing and sanctions for suspended sentence violation or new offense
headings.reviewNote: Requires a hearing (unless waived) upon probable cause that the offender violated a suspended-sentence condition or committed a new offense, permitting the court to continue or revoke the juvenile disposition, impose the adult sentence, or enter another order.

headings.title: Division of youth services petition to transfer custody beyond treatment
headings.reviewNote: Permits the division of youth services to petition for a transfer of custody when the child is beyond the scope of its treatment programs, requiring a hearing to either revoke suspension for department of corrections custody or place the offender on probation.

headings.title: Mandatory court hearing when offender reaches age eighteen
headings.reviewNote: Requires a hearing when an offender with a suspended sentence reaches age eighteen to revoke suspension for department of corrections custody, place on probation, or continue division of youth services custody if the division agrees.

headings.title: Division of youth services petition for hearing before release prior to 21
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division of youth services to petition for a hearing before releasing a subsection 1 offender before age twenty-one, requiring the court to either revoke suspension for department of corrections custody or place the offender on probation.

headings.title: Credit for time served in division of youth services custody
headings.reviewNote: Requires crediting all time served under the juvenile disposition toward the adult criminal sentence if suspension of the adult sentence is revoked.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 editorial headings for 211.073 governing dual jurisdiction blended sentencing, violation hearings, custody transfer petitions, age-eighteen hearings, pre-release hearings, and credit for time served.

headings.title: Preliminary inquiry, informal adjustment or petition, and out-of-state approval
headings.reviewNote: Requires a preliminary inquiry upon written referral under section 211.031, permits informal adjustment or petition filing, and bars out-of-state disposition placement without prior children's division approval.

headings.title: Institutional placement standards, evaluations, funding, and judge limits
headings.reviewNote: Requires least-restrictive institutional placement based on psychological/psychiatric evaluation, mandates pre-order findings and division funding certification or alternative placement, and bars the judge from ordering a specific provider while allowing designation of service scope and type.

headings.title: Fiscal-year appropriation cap on state obligations under section 211.181
headings.reviewNote: Provides that state obligations incurred under section 211.181 shall not exceed in any fiscal year the amount appropriated for that purpose.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 editorial headings for 211.081 governing preliminary inquiries and out-of-state placement approval, institutional placement evaluations and judge limits, and fiscal-year appropriation caps.

headings.title: Restitution and community service in informal adjustment agreements
headings.reviewNote: Permits the juvenile court in an informal adjustment under section 211.081 to allow the child to make reasonable restitution/reparation (with optional circuit clerk disbursement) or complete court-supervised community service.

headings.title: Immunity for community service supervisors and non-employee status
headings.reviewNote: Grants immunity from child or derivative suits to persons, organizations, agencies, and employees supervising or benefiting from services (excluding intentional torts or wanton, willful, or malicious conduct) and excludes the child from chapter 287 employee and chapter 288 employment status.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 editorial headings for 211.083 governing court-allowed restitution or community service in informal adjustments, supervisor immunity, and non-employee status.

headings.title: Court-ordered employment for restitution by adjudicated nonviolent youth
headings.reviewNote: Permits the court to order a child age fourteen or older adjudicated for a nonviolent crime to work for any employer at up to minimum wage for the time necessary to make restitution.

headings.title: Exclusion of working child from section 290.500 employee definition
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a child age fourteen or older ordered to work for restitution under subsection 1 is not considered an employee as defined in section 290.500.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 editorial headings for 211.085 governing court-ordered restitution employment for nonviolent adjudicated youth age fourteen or older and exclusion from section 290.500 employee status.

headings.title: Title and caption of petition in juvenile court
headings.reviewNote: Requires the petition to be entitled 'In the interest of _______, a child under eighteen years of age'.

headings.title: Required factual allegations and party details in petition
headings.reviewNote: Requires the petition to state plainly jurisdictional facts, the child's name, birth date, and residence, living parents' names and residences, guardian/custodian/nearest relative details, and other pertinent data.

headings.title: Statement of unknown facts in petition
headings.reviewNote: Requires the petition to state if any facts required in subsection 2 are unknown to the petitioner.

headings.title: Juvenile officer best interest assessment prior to voluntary dismissal
headings.reviewNote: Requires the juvenile officer, prior to voluntary dismissal of a petition, to assess the impact on the child's best interests and take all actions practicable to minimize any negative impact.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 editorial headings for 211.091 governing petition captions, required factual allegations, statements of unknown facts, and best-interest assessment before voluntary dismissal.

headings.title: Precedence of juvenile court orders over inconsistent civil custody decrees
headings.reviewNote: Provides that chapter 211 or 210 orders take precedence over inconsistent chapter 452, 453, 454, 455, or 475 orders regarding a child under twenty-one while the juvenile court exercises continuing jurisdiction.

headings.title: Authority to enter custody, support, visitation, and paternity orders
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes custody, child support, and visitation orders in section 211.031(1)(1) cases and grants concurrent authority with the circuit court to enter final paternity judgments under the uniform parentage act in section 211.031(1)(1) or (2) cases.

headings.title: Post-termination validity, stay of prior orders, and binding paternity judgment
headings.reviewNote: Keeps subsection 2 custody, support, and visitation orders in effect after juvenile proceedings end unless stated otherwise, stays prior inconsistent orders until superseded, and makes paternity judgments final and binding (optionally under a nonjuvenile case number).

headings.title: Custody reversion upon termination without continuing custody order
headings.reviewNote: Returns legal and physical custody to the prior custodian, parent, or guardian and restores prior custody or visitation orders if the juvenile court terminates jurisdiction without entering a continuing order under subsections 2 and 3.

headings.title: Prohibition on juvenile court hearing post-termination modification motions
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits the juvenile court from hearing modification or rehearing motions after terminating jurisdiction on the underlying case, directing future actions under sections 210.817 to 210.852 or chapters 211, 452, 453, 454, 455, or 475.

headings.title: Chapter 454 enforcement and family support division transmittal of support
headings.reviewNote: Requires juvenile child support orders to be established and enforced under chapter 454 and directs the circuit clerk to send a certified copy to the family support division for enforcement.

headings.title: Sixty-day reasonable efforts duty of children's division to establish paternity
headings.reviewNote: Requires the children's division in all section 211.031(1)(1) and (2) cases to make all reasonable efforts under section 211.183 to establish paternity within sixty days of the juvenile court obtaining jurisdiction.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 7 editorial headings for 211.093 governing precedence of juvenile court orders, custody/support/visitation and paternity authority, post-termination validity and reversion, modification limits, support enforcement, and 60-day paternity efforts.

headings.title: Issuance of summons requiring appearance of child custodian
headings.reviewNote: Directs juvenile court to issue summons requiring person having custody to appear personally with child for hearing.

headings.title: Notice to parents or guardians not having custody of child
headings.reviewNote: Requires notice of hearing date and case pendency to be given to non-custodial parents or guardians.

headings.title: Endorsement on summons ordering immediate temporary custody
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes judge to order immediate custody transfer by endorsement on summons when child welfare requires.

headings.title: Issuance of witness subpoenas by juvenile judge
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes court to issue subpoenas compelling attendance of any person whose presence is deemed necessary.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 editorial headings for 211.101 governing issuance of summons, notice to non-custodial parents or guardians, immediate temporary custody endorsement, and subpoenas.

headings.title: Personal service of summons and service by registered mail or publication
headings.reviewNote: Requires personal service of summons and authorizes registered mail or publication when personal delivery is impracticable.

headings.title: Time limits for personal service and registered mail prior to hearing
headings.reviewNote: Mandates personal service at least twenty-four hours before hearing and requires mail service at least five days prior.

headings.title: Persons authorized to execute service under direction of court
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes service of summons to be executed by any suitable person designated by the juvenile court.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 editorial headings for 211.111 governing personal, registered mail, and publication service of summons, pre-hearing time limits, and authorized process servers.

headings.title: Taking child into custody not deemed an arrest
headings.reviewNote: Provides that taking a child into custody under juvenile code authority does not constitute a criminal arrest.

headings.title: Notice to parent, legal custodian, or guardian as soon as possible
headings.reviewNote: Requires that when a child is taken into custody, the child's parent, legal custodian, or guardian be notified as soon as possible.

headings.title: Attachment of juvenile court jurisdiction from time child is taken into custody
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that juvenile court jurisdiction attaches immediately at the moment the child is taken into custody.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 editorial headings for 211.131 governing non-arrest status of taking a child into custody, notice to parents or custodians, and attachment of jurisdiction.

headings.title: Court authority to order parental participation in treatment activities
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the court to require parent or guardian participation in counseling, treatment, or rehabilitation activities.

headings.title: Order requiring parent to pay institutional maintenance and support costs
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the court to order parent or guardian to pay reasonable support and treatment costs for institutionalized child.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 editorial headings for 211.134 governing discretionary court orders requiring parental participation in treatment activities and institutional support payments.

headings.title: Standards for ordering appearance of child in court
headings.reviewNote: Requires the court, after considering children's division information and family support team input, to order the child to appear only if necessary to make a decision and after weighing courtroom trauma and disruption/hardship, in compliance with federal guidelines.

headings.title: Preservation of child's right to attend hearing under section 210.564
headings.reviewNote: Provides that nothing in this section interferes with a child's right to attend a hearing under subdivision (7) of subsection 3 of section 210.564.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 editorial headings for 211.135 governing limits on ordering a child's court appearance and preserving the child's hearing attendance right under section 210.564.

headings.title: Release of child to custody of parent or custodian upon promise to appear
headings.reviewNote: Requires returning a child taken into custody to the parent, guardian, or legal custodian on a promise to appear (with optional signed written promise) unless otherwise ordered, and permits additional court conditions with notice that noncompliance may lead to detention.

headings.title: Conditional release or detention on order of court
headings.reviewNote: Permits conditional release or detention under section 211.151 only on court order specifying the reason, and requires notifying the parent, guardian, or legal custodian as soon as possible.

headings.title: Twenty-four-hour conditional release or detention by juvenile officer
headings.reviewNote: Permits the juvenile officer to conditionally release or detain a child up to twenty-four hours when obtaining a written court order is impractical due to hour, Sunday, or holiday, requires a written record and report, and requires another circuit judge's approval to continue past twenty-four hours if the judge is absent.

headings.title: Mandatory risk and needs assessment prior to disposition
headings.reviewNote: Requires the juvenile officer in any section 211.031 referral to make and report a standardized OSCA-approved risk and needs assessment before disposition.

headings.title: Biennial random sampling review of assessments and dispositions
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division, with juvenile officers and juvenile courts, to review a random sample of assessments and dispositions at least biennially to recommend statewide equity, identify racial disparity in certification, and protect case confidentiality.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 editorial headings for 211.141 governing release on promise to appear, court-ordered conditional release or detention, 24-hour juvenile officer authority, risk/needs assessments, and biennial sampling reviews.

headings.title: Authorized places of temporary juvenile detention pending disposition
headings.reviewNote: Permits written court orders pending disposition detaining a child in a county juvenile detention facility, supervised shelter care facility, child-protection association facility, or other suitable custody.

headings.title: Prohibition on detaining child in adult jail or holding facility
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits detaining a child in a jail or adult detention facility pending disposition of a juvenile case.

headings.title: Fingerprinting, photographing, record closure, and expungement rules
headings.reviewNote: Requires law enforcement to fingerprint and photograph children taken into custody for felony-equivalent offenses without judge approval, permits doing so with judge consent for abuse/neglect, status, or misdemeanor cases, closes records if no petition is filed within thirty days, and allows expungement after one year.

headings.title: Definitions of adult detention facility and juvenile detention facility
headings.reviewNote: Defines jail or other adult detention facility and juvenile detention facility, including spatial, program, and staff separation requirements when located in the same building or grounds.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 editorial headings for 211.151 governing authorized detention places, adult jail prohibition, fingerprinting/photographing and record closure/expungement, and facility definitions.

headings.title: State contribution toward county institutional home child maintenance
headings.reviewNote: Requires the state to pay counties fourteen to thirty-seven dollars per day, subject to appropriations, upon circuit court order or voucher for care and maintenance in county homes for neglected and delinquent children.

headings.title: State reimbursement to counties for temporary juvenile detention costs
headings.reviewNote: Requires the state to pay county governing bodies fourteen to thirty-seven dollars per day, subject to appropriations, upon certified circuit court voucher or order for children detained under section 211.151.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 editorial headings for 211.156 governing state per diem payments ($14 to $37 per day, subject to appropriations) to counties for institutional homes and section 211.151 detention.

headings.title: Court-ordered medical, psychiatric, and psychological examinations
headings.reviewNote: Permits the court to order examination of a child by an appointed physician, psychiatrist, or psychologist, with court-approved expenses paid by the county except for department of mental health direct or contract examinations.

headings.title: Utilization of public hospitals and psychiatric clinics for examinations
headings.reviewNote: Permits court to utilize services of state, county, or municipal hospitals and mental clinics for diagnostic evaluations.

headings.title: County authority to establish juvenile diagnostic and treatment facilities
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes counties to establish medical and psychiatric facilities to assist juvenile courts with diagnosis and treatment.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 editorial headings for 211.161 governing court-ordered physical and mental examinations, use of public hospitals/clinics, and county diagnostic and treatment facilities.

headings.title: Juvenile hearing procedures and discretion of judge
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes juvenile judge to determine hearing formality consistent with statutory and constitutional due process standards.

headings.title: Proceeding in absence of child and adjournments
headings.reviewNote: Permits court to conduct hearing in absence of child and adjourn proceedings as justice requires.

headings.title: Notice, standing, writ relief, and protection for foster parents and relatives
headings.reviewNote: Requires notice and opportunity to be heard for current foster parents, preadoptive parents, and caretaking relatives, grants foster parents standing and fee-free remedial writ relief under rules 84, 94, and 97, and bars removal solely for filing or pendency of a writ unless needed for health and safety.

headings.title: Foster parent access to child medical and psychological records
headings.reviewNote: Requires the court to inquire at the first hearing where a foster parent is present to ensure full access to the child's medical, psychological, and psychiatric records from the children's division and contractors under section 210.566.

headings.title: Separate hearing of juvenile cases from adult criminal trials
headings.reviewNote: Requires juvenile cases to be heard separately from adult court proceedings and docketed independently.

headings.title: Stenographic recording of juvenile court proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Requires court reporter stenographic notes or authorized recordings upon court order or request of any interested party.

headings.title: Exclusion of general public and specified felony exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Excludes the general public and admits only persons with a direct interest, except for class A or B felony conduct or class C felony conduct with two or more prior unrelated class A, B, or C felony adjudications.

headings.title: Applicability of equity practice and limits on hearing continuances
headings.reviewNote: Applies customary equity practice and procedure, except prohibiting continuances absent compelling extenuating circumstances with specific written findings on the record.

headings.title: Right of crime victim to submit written statement and attend hearing
headings.reviewNote: Requires allowing a crime victim to submit a written statement and appear personally or by counsel (unless presence would not serve justice) limited to case facts, injuries, or financial loss, and permits immediate family appearance if the victim died or is unable to appear.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 9 editorial headings for 211.171 governing hearing procedures, child absence, foster parent standing and medical record access, separate hearings, recording, public exclusion, equity practice and continuances, and victim statements.

headings.title: Grandparent statutory right to intervene in custody proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Grants grandparents right to intervene in juvenile proceedings involving custody of grandchild absent judicial finding against child.

headings.title: Permissive termination of grandparent intervention right upon adoption
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a grandparent's right to intervene may terminate upon adoption of the child, except when adopted by a stepparent, another grandparent, or other blood relative.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 editorial headings for 211.177 governing grandparent right to intervene in custody proceedings and permissive termination of that right upon adoption.

headings.title: Dispositional decrees and placement options for neglected children
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes dispositional orders for section 211.031(1)(1) children including supervised placement, agency custody (excluding DYS), medical/psychiatric treatment (with remedial treatment exception), least-restrictive individualized treatment plans, and federal waiver applications.

headings.title: Dispositional orders, probation, and up to ten-dollar child assessment
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes dispositional orders for section 211.031(1)(2) status offenders including supervision, custody (DYS only if already under supervision), treatment, up to ten-dollar assessment paid by the child, and suspended execution with revocable probation.

headings.title: Dispositional orders, restitution, community service, and assessments
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes dispositional orders for section 211.031(1)(3) delinquents including supervision (with 1,000-foot sex-offense residence ban and sibling/same-home exception), custody, DYS length-of-stay directions, license suspension, restitution, community service with supervisor immunity and non-employee status, probation, and $25/$50 assessments.

headings.title: Minimum institutional custody periods for youth services commitments
headings.reviewNote: Permits setting a minimum DYS custody period beginning January 1, 1996 (not exceeding age nineteen absent a section 219.021(1) petition), bars early discharge without court order, allows DYS early-discharge petitions for good cause, and permits discharge or lawful retention after completion.

headings.title: Payment of assessments into section 211.185 judgment fund
headings.reviewNote: Requires assessments imposed under subsection 2 or 3 to be paid to the circuit court clerk for deposit in a fund established solely for paying judgments entered against children under section 211.185.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 editorial headings for 211.181 governing dispositional orders for care/neglect, status, and delinquency cases, minimum youth services commitment periods, and assessment fund deposits.

headings.title: Mandatory judicial determination of division reasonable efforts
headings.reviewNote: Requires removal orders to determine whether the children's division made reasonable efforts to prevent removal and enable return home, and deems reasonable efforts made when first family contact occurred during an emergency where the child could not safely remain home.

headings.title: Statutory definition of reasonable efforts and health paramountcy
headings.reviewNote: Defines reasonable efforts as diligent exercise of care to preserve family, keeping child health and safety paramount.

headings.title: Required factual findings supporting reasonable efforts determination
headings.reviewNote: Requires court to enter specific factual findings detailing preventive and reunification services provided to family.

headings.title: Emergency removal authorization when efforts could not ensure safety
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes court to order child removal even if division efforts were incomplete when further efforts would compromise safety.

headings.title: Prerequisite child safety and services findings prior to home removal
headings.reviewNote: Requires written findings that continuation in home is contrary to welfare and services cannot sufficiently protect child.

headings.title: Steps to modify permanency plan when efforts conflict with permanency
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division, if continuing reasonable efforts is inconsistent with permanent placement, to take necessary steps including seeking court order modification of the child's permanency plan.

headings.title: Statutory exceptions where reasonable efforts are not required
headings.reviewNote: Relieves the division of mandatory reasonable efforts (while preserving discretion) when a court determines severe/recurrent abuse, murder or voluntary manslaughter of another child (or attempt/conspiracy/solicitation), felony assault causing serious bodily injury, or involuntary termination of parental rights to a sibling.

headings.title: Mandatory permanency hearing within thirty days of effort waiver
headings.reviewNote: Requires court to conduct a permanency hearing within thirty days after determining reasonable efforts are not required.

headings.title: Concurrent planning for permanent placement during reunification efforts
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes children's division to engage in concurrent permanency planning while simultaneously pursuing family reunification.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 9 editorial headings for 211.183 governing reasonable efforts determinations, definitions, findings, emergency removal, pre-removal order contents, permanency plan modification, exceptions, 30-day permanency hearings, and concurrent planning.

headings.title: Court authority to order restitution against child and parents
headings.reviewNote: Empowers juvenile court to enter restitution judgment against delinquent child and parents for offense-related damages.

headings.title: Eligible recipients of court-ordered restitution judgments
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes restitution payments to crime victims, government entities, and third-party payors or insurers.

headings.title: Priority of restitution payments to crime victims over third-party payors
headings.reviewNote: Grants crime victims absolute payment priority over third-party insurance payors in restitution disbursements.

headings.title: Priority of victim restitution over government entity claims
headings.reviewNote: Mandates that victim restitution claims be satisfied in full prior to any disbursements to governmental bodies.

headings.title: Direct personal restitution by child to wronged victim
headings.reviewNote: Permits court to order juvenile to make restitution payments directly to the victim based on child's age and resources.

headings.title: Restitution hearing within thirty days of disposition
headings.reviewNote: Requires a restitution hearing within thirty days after disposition (extendable for good cause) and makes written medical, dental, hospital, funeral, or burial bills prima facie evidence of fair and reasonable charges.

headings.title: Procedural due process rights of parents at restitution hearing
headings.reviewNote: Bars a restitution judgment against a parent without reasonable opportunity to be heard and present evidence, requires advising the parent of the right to obtain counsel, and permits holding the hearing during adjudication or disposition.

headings.title: Enforcement of restitution judgments as civil monetary judgments
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes enforcement of juvenile restitution judgments in the same manner as civil money judgments.

headings.title: Preservation of civil actions and four-thousand-dollar total cap
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that a restitution judgment does not bar a section 537.045 or 8.150 proceeding for unpaid balance, but caps total restitution under this section, section 8.150, and section 537.045 at four thousand dollars.

headings.title: Community service work credit toward juvenile restitution obligations
headings.reviewNote: Allows child to perform court-approved community service with hourly compensation credited toward restitution balance.

headings.title: Execution of restitution judgment against child after age eighteen
headings.reviewNote: Permits executing a restitution judgment entered against a child under this section after the child attains age eighteen.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 11 editorial headings for 211.185 governing restitution judgments against parents and children, recipients, victim priority, hearings, enforcement, $4,000 cap, community service credits, and execution at age eighteen.

headings.title: Court order requiring nonviolent child to work for restitution
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes juvenile court to order nonviolent adjudicated youth age fourteen or older to work to earn restitution funds.

headings.title: Exemption from statutory employee definition for restitution work
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a child age fourteen or older ordered to make restitution under subsection 1 is not considered an employee as defined in section 290.500.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 editorial headings for 211.188 governing court-ordered restitution work for nonviolent adjudicated children age fourteen or older and exclusion from section 290.500 employee status.

headings.title: Thirty-day limit on mental health placements outside statutory procedures
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits the juvenile court from ordering children detained by, committed to, or placed in the department of mental health for periods longer than thirty days except as provided in sections 211.201 to 211.207.

headings.title: Loss of juvenile court jurisdiction upon commitment unless expressly retained
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a juvenile court loses jurisdiction of a child committed to the department of mental health unless the commitment order expressly retains jurisdiction.

headings.title: Extension of mental health detention beyond eighteenth birthday
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits detaining a child in department custody beyond the eighteenth birthday without an express court order after a hearing within thirty days of the birthday, following thirty-day advance discharge notice from the department.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 editorial headings for 211.201 governing thirty-day limit on department of mental health placements outside sections 211.201 to 211.207, loss of juvenile court jurisdiction unless retained, and detention beyond age eighteen.

headings.title: Referral of child to department of mental health for evaluation
headings.reviewNote: Permits the juvenile court, on its own motion or an interested party's motion or petition, to order a department of mental health evaluation of a child appearing mentally disordered (other than intellectually or developmentally disabled).

headings.title: Twenty-day evaluation and criteria for inpatient mental health admission
headings.reviewNote: Requires a designated mental health facility to evaluate the child within twenty days (outpatient if practicable) to determine whether four statutory inpatient admission criteria are met.

headings.title: Court order committing mentally disordered child for inpatient treatment
headings.reviewNote: Requires admission recommendation and notice if inpatient care is appropriate, grants a right to independent evaluation, and permits commitment for inpatient care and treatment within twenty days after a hearing.

headings.title: Notice and transfer or hearing when inpatient admission is inappropriate
headings.reviewNote: Requires notice and evaluation copy within twenty days when inpatient admission is not appropriate, and if evaluated inpatient, requires the juvenile court to transfer the child or set a noticed hearing within twenty days.

headings.title: Referral for section 630.610 placement or discharge when inpatient care ends
headings.reviewNote: Requires referral and placement under section 630.610 (or discharge/other safe arrangements if unavailable) when inpatient care is no longer appropriate, with notice sent to the juvenile court.

headings.title: Annual juvenile court review of continued mental health placement
headings.reviewNote: Requires the committing juvenile court to conduct an annual review of the child's need for continued placement in the mental health facility.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 editorial headings for 211.202 governing mental health evaluations, inpatient admission criteria, commitment orders, inappropriate-admission transfers, section 630.610 placement or discharge, and annual court reviews.

headings.title: Court order for mental health department developmental evaluation
headings.reviewNote: Permits the juvenile court, on its own motion or an interested party's motion or petition, to order the department of mental health to evaluate a child appearing intellectually disabled or developmentally disabled under chapter 630.

headings.title: Evaluation report and recommendation for developmental disability placement
headings.reviewNote: Directs regional center to report whether child requires residential habilitation or community developmental services.

headings.title: Court order committing child to residential developmental disability facility
headings.reviewNote: Requires admission recommendation and notice if residential care is appropriate, grants independent evaluation rights, permits commitment within twenty days after a hearing, and requires a six-day due process hearing and notice if proposing placement or transfer to a different department facility.

headings.title: Notice and five-day transfer or twenty-day hearing if admission inappropriate
headings.reviewNote: Requires regional center notice and evaluation copy when admission is inappropriate, and if evaluated on a residential basis, requires transfer within five days or a noticed hearing within twenty days.

headings.title: Referral for section 630.610 placement or discharge from habilitation
headings.reviewNote: Requires referral and placement under section 630.610 (or discharge/other safe arrangements if unavailable) when residential habilitation is no longer appropriate, with notice to the juvenile court.

headings.title: Annual judicial review of developmental disability residential placement
headings.reviewNote: Mandates annual court review of child's continuing necessity for residential developmental habilitation.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 editorial headings for 211.203 governing evaluations of intellectually or developmentally disabled children, regional center referrals, commitment and transfer hearings, inappropriate-admission transfers, section 630.610 placement or discharge, and annual reviews.

headings.title: Individualized treatment or habilitation plan for committed child
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department of mental health director or designee to prepare an individualized treatment or habilitation plan within thirty days of admission, review status at least every thirty days, and send copies to the committing juvenile court.

headings.title: Mandatory discharge by department of mental health upon specified findings
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department of mental health to discharge a committed child if the facility head or designee determines in an evaluation or periodic review that any of five statutory conditions are met.

headings.title: Notice of discharge to court when jurisdiction specifically retained
headings.reviewNote: Requires forwarding discharge notice with diagnosis and placement recommendations at least twenty days before discharge when jurisdiction was retained, and terminates court jurisdiction after twenty days unless the court orders the child brought before it.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 editorial headings for 211.206 governing individualized treatment or habilitation plans, mandatory discharge criteria, and twenty-day discharge notice when jurisdiction is retained.

headings.title: Mandatory youth services referral for mental health evaluation
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division of youth services to refer a committed child appearing mentally disordered to the department of mental health for a twenty-day evaluation (outpatient if practicable) of mental health or developmental disability placement criteria.

headings.title: Return of evaluated child to youth services upon negative finding
headings.reviewNote: Requires notifying the division of youth services director and returning an inpatient or residentially evaluated child if the department of mental health determines inpatient care or residential habilitation is not required.

headings.title: Discretionary transfer of physical custody to department of mental health
headings.reviewNote: Requires notice when admission is appropriate, permits the division of youth services director to transfer physical custody to the department of mental health for a mental health or developmental disability facility, and requires acceptance subject to suitable accommodations.

headings.title: Treatment or habilitation plan, thirty-day reviews, and return to custody
headings.reviewNote: Requires an individualized treatment or habilitation plan, reviews at least every thirty days, and notification and return of the child to division of youth services custody if inpatient care or residential habilitation is no longer appropriate.

headings.title: Retention of transferred child following expiration of youth services custody
headings.reviewNote: Provides that if a child ceases to come under division of youth services jurisdiction, the child may be retained in a mental health or developmental disability facility only as otherwise provided by law.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 editorial headings for 211.207 governing mandatory youth services referrals for mental health evaluation, return upon negative finding, custody transfers, treatment plans and reviews, and retention after jurisdiction ends.

headings.title: Statutory right of child to legal counsel and guardian ad litem
headings.reviewNote: Entitles a child to counsel in section 211.031(1)(2) and (3) proceedings and a guardian ad litem in section 211.031(1)(1) proceedings, except under section 210.160(3) where non-waivable counsel shall be appointed.

headings.title: Appointment of counsel prior to filing of formal petition
headings.reviewNote: Mandates court appointment of counsel for child prior to petition filing upon request and showing of indigency.

headings.title: Discretionary counsel appointment and formal waiver requirements
headings.reviewNote: Permits appointing counsel in section 211.031(1)(2) or (3) cases unless private counsel appears or counsel is waived (subject to subsection 10 consultation/hearing limits), and requires any waiver to be in open court, recorded, in writing, and knowing, intelligent, and voluntary under the totality of circumstances.

headings.title: Appointment of counsel for indigent parents or custodians
headings.reviewNote: Requires court to appoint attorney for child's indigent custodian in proceedings threatening parental custody rights.

headings.title: Reasonable preparation time for appointed counsel
headings.reviewNote: Requires court to grant appointed counsel reasonable time to investigate facts and prepare for juvenile hearings.

headings.title: Continuity of representation through all stages and appeals
headings.reviewNote: Provides that counsel serves through all stages including appeals unless relieved by the court for good cause.

headings.title: Dual representation of child and custodian and conflict of interest
headings.reviewNote: Permits joint representation of child and custodian but mandates separate counsel whenever interests conflict.

headings.title: Standards for judicial approval of waiver of counsel by child
headings.reviewNote: Allows child to waive counsel only with court approval after determining waiver is knowing, voluntary, and permitted by law.

headings.title: Withdrawal of counsel waiver at any stage of proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes child to withdraw waiver of counsel at any time, requiring immediate appointment of counsel by the court.

headings.title: Proceedings where waiver of counsel by child is strictly prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Bars waiver of counsel at contested felony detention hearings (unless agreement is reached), certification/Rule 129.04 dismissal hearings, felony adjudication or misdemeanor/felony modification/revocation detention hearings, dispositional hearings, and supervision modification/revocation hearings.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 10 editorial headings for 211.211 governing right to counsel and guardian ad litem, pre-petition and post-petition appointments, waiver requirements, custodian counsel, preparation, continuity, conflicts, withdrawal, and non-waivable proceedings.

headings.title: Indeterminate duration of juvenile court commitments and age limits
headings.reviewNote: Provides that juvenile court commitments are indeterminate—unless committed under section 211.181(3)(3)—and shall not continue beyond the child's twenty-first birthday.

headings.title: Transmission of social history and institutional summary records
headings.reviewNote: Requires court to transmit social summary to receiving institution and directs institution to share treatment progress records.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 editorial headings for 211.231 governing indeterminate commitments with section 211.181(3)(3) exception and age-21 limit, and information exchange between court and institutions.

headings.title: Court summons to parent to show cause regarding child support
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes court to examine parent's financial ability and issue summons to show cause regarding support contributions.

headings.title: Order requiring parental contribution to child support and maintenance
headings.reviewNote: Permits the court, upon finding a parent able to support or contribute to a child's support, to order support or contribution and payment of judgment collection costs.

headings.title: Enforcement of child support order by execution on property
headings.reviewNote: Permits enforcement by execution on request of the juvenile officer or custodian without cost deposit or bond, eliminates property exemptions, and subjects all wages or sums due the parent to garnishment or execution.

headings.title: County liability for necessary child support upon parental inability
headings.reviewNote: Directs necessary support of committed child to be paid from county funds when parents are financially unable to pay.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 editorial headings for 211.241 governing parental support inquiries and summons, support and collection-cost orders, execution without exemptions, and county support upon judicial approval.

headings.title: Modification of juvenile court dispositional decree on court motion
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes juvenile court to modify any dispositional decree at any time upon its own motion.

headings.title: Petition by juvenile officer, parent, or relative to modify decree
headings.reviewNote: Permits juvenile officer, parents, guardians, or relatives to petition court for modification or termination of custody decree.

headings.title: Limitation on modification authority over youth services commitments
headings.reviewNote: Subordinates juvenile court decree modification authority over children committed to youth services to chapter 219.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 editorial headings for 211.251 governing modification of dispositional decrees on court motion, petitions to modify custody orders, and subordination to chapter 219.

headings.title: Appeals from final judgments by child, parent, or juvenile officer
headings.reviewNote: Allows appeals from final judgments, orders, or decrees by the child, an adversely affected parent, or the juvenile officer (except final determinations under section 211.031(1)(3)), with a thirty-day notice deadline and no automatic supersedeas.

headings.title: Interlocutory appeals from suppression or placement modification orders
headings.reviewNote: Allows interlocutory appeal by the juvenile officer from orders suppressing evidence, confessions, or admissions under section 211.031(1)(3), or by a parent, guardian ad litem, child's counsel, or juvenile officer from orders changing or modifying child placement.

headings.title: Procedure, notice, and appellate time limits for interlocutory appeals
headings.reviewNote: Directs subsection 2 interlocutory appeals to the Missouri court of appeals with a three-day notice deadline and the same time limits as state interlocutory appeals in criminal cases.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 editorial headings for 211.261 governing final-judgment appeals by child, parent, or juvenile officer, interlocutory appeals from suppression or placement orders, and three-day interlocutory appeal timelines.

headings.title: Adjudication not deemed criminal conviction or civil disability
headings.reviewNote: Affirms that juvenile court adjudication is not a criminal conviction and imposes no civil or political disabilities.

headings.title: Prohibition on criminal charges absent adult transfer order
headings.reviewNote: Bars charging or prosecuting child with a crime unless case is transferred to court of general jurisdiction.

headings.title: Inadmissibility of juvenile statements, evidence, and records outside chapter
headings.reviewNote: Bars using a child's post-custody statements to juvenile personnel, chapter 211 evidence, and juvenile court reports and records against the child in any civil or criminal proceeding other than chapter 211 proceedings.

headings.title: Preservation of eligibility for civil and military service
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that juvenile court disposition does not disqualify youth from civil service appointments or military enlistment.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 editorial headings for 211.271 governing non-criminal status of adjudications, bar on criminal charges absent transfer, inadmissibility of juvenile statements/records outside chapter 211, and civil/military eligibility.

headings.title: Designation of juvenile courtroom in first and second class counties
headings.reviewNote: Requires first and second class counties and St. Louis city to provide a designated juvenile courtroom.

headings.title: Performance of juvenile duties by circuit judges during absence
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes any circuit judge within the judicial circuit to hold juvenile court in the judge's absence or inability.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 editorial headings for 211.291 governing juvenile courtrooms in first and second class counties and St. Louis city and substitute circuit judges.

headings.title: Chambers hearings in third and fourth class counties
headings.reviewNote: Permits juvenile hearings in third and fourth class counties to be conducted in judicial chambers or designated rooms.

headings.title: Substitute judge assignment and multicounty circuit authority
headings.reviewNote: Permits an absent or unable juvenile judge to request supreme court assignment of another circuit judge, and permits a multicounty juvenile judge to act on a circuit juvenile case from anywhere within the circuit.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 editorial headings for 211.301 governing chambers hearings in third and fourth class counties, supreme court judge assignments, and multicounty circuit authority.

headings.title: Open court proceedings in child abuse, neglect, and termination cases
headings.reviewNote: Opens section 211.031(1)(1) and juvenile officer/division termination proceedings to the public on or before July 1, 2005, except closed hearings for written consent under section 453.010(6), and governs court-initiated or non-state party closure motions.

headings.title: Exclusion of general public during testimony of child witness
headings.reviewNote: Mandates closure of courtroom to general public during testimony of child victim or witness in abuse proceedings.

headings.title: Public access to pleadings and orders in child protection cases
headings.reviewNote: Makes pleadings and orders in abuse and neglect cases open for public inspection unless specifically closed by court order.

headings.title: Redaction of child and child-abuse reporter identities in public records
headings.reviewNote: Requires redacting the identity of any child involved except the perpetrator prior to public disclosure and prohibits disclosing information that may identify a child abuse reporter under sections 210.109 to 210.183 and 352.400.

headings.title: Closure of delinquency proceedings to general public
headings.reviewNote: Directs that juvenile delinquency proceedings under section 211.031 shall remain closed to the general public.

headings.title: Applicability to child protection proceedings filed on or after July 1, 2005
headings.reviewNote: Applies open hearing and public access provisions to child protection cases commenced on or after July 1, 2005.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 editorial headings for 211.319 governing open abuse/neglect and termination proceedings, child/victim testimony closure, public pleadings/orders, identity redaction, closed delinquency proceedings, and July 1, 2005 applicability.

headings.title: Confidentiality of juvenile court proceedings and social records
headings.reviewNote: Protects juvenile court legal and social records from public inspection except upon court order or statutory exception.

headings.title: Confidentiality and disclosure rules for status and delinquency records
headings.reviewNote: Keeps section 211.031(1)(2) records confidential absent court order or statute, and for section 211.031(1)(3) cases authorizes juvenile officer sharing with listed persons/agencies, non-identifying public updates, and open felony dispositional hearing records while keeping social summaries and status reports confidential.

headings.title: Maintenance and confidentiality of peace officer juvenile records
headings.reviewNote: Requires keeping peace officers' juvenile records separate and confidential absent court order, except for section 211.071 transfers, convictions under sections 578.421 to 578.437, and civil forfeiture actions under section 195.140.

headings.title: Release of non-identifying statistical information to authorized entities
headings.reviewNote: Permits compilation and release of non-identifying statistical data regarding juvenile justice administration.

headings.title: Destruction of social records and sealing of court and police files
headings.reviewNote: Permits ordering destruction of social histories/records other than the official court file and sealing of the official court file and peace officers' records after age eighteen (or after case closing if jurisdiction continues) when in the child's best interest.

headings.title: Release of general disposition information to crime victims or family
headings.reviewNote: Permits releasing general information regarding informal adjustment or formal adjudication disposition to a victim or immediate family member, excluding specific location/duration of treatment or detention or supervision terms.

headings.title: Disclosure of juvenile records to child fatality review panels
headings.reviewNote: Requires disclosing juvenile court proceedings and social records to the child fatality review panel under section 210.192 unless the juvenile court enters an order sealing the victim child's records.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 7 editorial headings for 211.321 governing juvenile court record confidentiality, subdivision (2) and (3) disclosure exceptions, peace officer records, statistics, destruction/sealing after age eighteen, victim updates, and child fatality panels.

headings.title: Development of performance standards and diversion program evaluations
headings.reviewNote: Directs state courts administrator to establish juvenile court performance standards, risk tools, and diversion evaluations.

headings.title: Evaluation of racial disparities in juvenile justice system standards
headings.reviewNote: Requires performance standards, training programs, and risk assessment forms to address and reduce racial disparities.

headings.title: Mandatory annual training on sex trafficking and human trafficking
headings.reviewNote: Requires continuing education standards to include one hour of annual sex and human trafficking training for each juvenile officer under section 210.1505 guidelines; effective January 1, 2027, and expires December 31, 2031.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 editorial headings for 211.326 governing state courts administrator standards and training, consideration of racial disparities, and annual trafficking training effective 2027 through 2031.

headings.title: County duty to provide juvenile detention facilities and court offices
headings.reviewNote: Requires governing bodies of first and second classification counties and any city not within a county to provide a juvenile detention facility and offices for juvenile court personnel.

headings.title: Complete physical and visual separation from adult inmates
headings.reviewNote: Mandates that juvenile detention facilities ensure children have no contact at any time with adult inmates.

headings.title: Appointment and compensation of detention facility superintendent
headings.reviewNote: Directs juvenile court judge to appoint detention facility superintendent and personnel, with county paying salaries.

headings.title: County authority to acquire land and construct detention buildings
