headings.reviewNote: Authorizes county governing bodies to purchase, lease, or construct land and buildings for juvenile detention facilities.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 editorial headings for 211.331 governing county detention facilities and court offices, separation from adults, superintendent appointment, and land/building acquisition (Revisor's Note notes H.B. 2637 & 3155 repealed S.B. 888's 2026 version effective 8-28-26).

headings.title: Circuit detention facilities by judge recommendation or county agreement
headings.reviewNote: Requires third and fourth class counties in a circuit to establish a juvenile detention facility and juvenile officer offices upon presiding judge written recommendation or county notice of all-county approval and a section 211.342 agreement.

headings.title: Hearing on necessity and feasibility before establishing facility
headings.reviewNote: Requires thirty days' notice and public hearing to determine need and financing before establishing detention facility.

headings.title: Operation, population-based cost proration, and facility location
headings.reviewNote: Applies section 211.331 to operation and maintenance, prorates establishment and operation costs among circuit counties by respective county populations, and sets location by presiding judge or section 211.342 agreement.

headings.title: Joint detention facilities for adjoining judicial circuits
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes presiding judges of adjoining judicial circuits to combine resources and establish a shared detention facility.

headings.title: Independent detention facilities in third and fourth class counties
headings.reviewNote: Allows third or fourth class counties to establish independent detention facilities under first-class county procedures.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 editorial headings for 211.341 governing third and fourth class county detention facilities, hearings, population-based cost proration, multi-circuit facilities, and independent facilities (Revisor's Note notes H.B. 2637 & 3155 repealed S.B. 888's 2026 version effective 8-28-26).

headings.title: Inter-county coordination to establish circuit juvenile detention facility
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes governing bodies of counties within same judicial circuit to coordinate and establish a joint detention center.

headings.title: Cooperative agreements between adjoining judicial circuits for detention
headings.reviewNote: Permits governing bodies in adjoining judicial circuits to establish and operate joint regional detention facilities.

headings.title: Notice of cooperative detention agreement to presiding judges
headings.reviewNote: Requires county governing bodies to notify presiding circuit judges before executing joint detention agreements.

headings.title: Required provisions and cost-sharing formulas in inter-county agreements
headings.reviewNote: Specifies five mandatory agreement provisions: total establishment/operation cost, population-based contribution formula, construction/leasing/financing methods and powers, subsection 6 sales tax use, and facility location.

headings.title: Operation, staffing, and judicial supervision of cooperative facilities
headings.reviewNote: Applies statutory staffing and judicial supervision provisions to cooperative juvenile detention centers.

headings.title: County sales tax authorization for juvenile detention and facilities
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes up to a one percent voter-approved county sales tax (with statutory ballot table and twelve-month resubmission limit), creates the special county trust fund and Juvenile Detention Facility Sales Tax Trust Fund, sets a one percent state collection fee, and governs refunds and ninety-day repeal notice.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 editorial headings for 211.342 governing inter-county and multi-circuit detention facility agreements, presiding judge notice, mandatory agreement terms, judicial governance, and dedicated sales tax with ballot table (Revisor's Note notes H.B. 2637 & 3155 repealed S.B. 888's 2026 version effective 8-28-26).

headings.title: Appointment and administrative authority over juvenile officers
headings.reviewNote: Directs juvenile court judge or family court administrator to appoint juvenile officers and personnel.

headings.title: Prohibition on appointing judge presiding over juvenile officer cases
headings.reviewNote: Bars judge who serves as appointing authority from presiding over cases in which juvenile officer is a participant.

headings.title: Population-based proration of juvenile court personnel costs
headings.reviewNote: Requires total county compensation costs for circuit or multi-circuit juvenile officers and personnel under subsection 1(1) and (2) to be prorated among counties by respective county populations.

headings.title: Circuit court grievance review committee for personnel actions
headings.reviewNote: Requires circuit court en banc to appoint a grievance committee to serve as final administrative authority for staff.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 editorial headings for 211.351 governing appointment of juvenile officers, presiding-judge conflict separation, population-based cost proration, and circuit grievance review committees.

headings.title: Creation, purpose, and membership of juvenile justice advisory board
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Missouri State Juvenile Justice Advisory Board within the office of state courts administrator to advise on best practices and juvenile officer standards, and specifies its nine appointed members and six ex officio voting members.

headings.title: Four-year terms, reappointment, vacancies, and uncompensated service
headings.reviewNote: Sets four-year terms with consecutive reappointment eligibility, directs filling vacancies for unexpired terms in the original manner, and provides that board members serve without compensation.

headings.title: Election of board chairperson and secretary
headings.reviewNote: Directs the advisory board membership to elect a chairperson and secretary from its ranks.

headings.title: Quarterly meeting requirement for advisory board
headings.reviewNote: Mandates that the advisory board meet at least four times per calendar year.

headings.title: Annual report of recommendations to state courts administrator and legislature
headings.reviewNote: Requires the board to provide a written annual report of recommendations and activities to the office of state courts administrator, office of child advocate, and joint committee on child abuse and neglect.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 editorial headings for 211.355 creating the Missouri state juvenile justice advisory board and governing its membership, four-year terms, officers, meetings, and annual report.

headings.title: Competitive examination and qualification standards for juvenile officers
headings.reviewNote: Requires the appointing court or family court administrator either to hold open competitive written and oral exams by court rule for qualified candidates or to appoint a person over age twenty-one with four years of sociology/related college education or four or more years of juvenile social work experience.

headings.title: Preservation of existing terms of office for incumbent juvenile officers
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that statutory qualification requirements do not terminate existing appointments or incumbent terms of office.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 editorial headings for 211.361 governing juvenile officer qualification options (competitive exam or education/experience) and preservation of incumbent terms.

headings.title: Annual statutory salary schedules for juvenile court personnel
headings.reviewNote: Establishes base annual statutory compensation schedules for juvenile officers and deputy juvenile officers.

headings.title: 1985 judicial-department salary adjustment and 1986 salary increase
headings.reviewNote: Increases subsection 1 salaries on September 28, 1985, by the fiscal year 1985 judicial-department adjustment under section 476.405, and increases salaries on January 1, 1986, to the subsection 1 amounts.

headings.title: Additional salary adjustments approved after September 28, 1985
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes juvenile officers to receive additional salary adjustments approved pursuant to chapter 476.

headings.title: Reimbursement of official travel expenses and mileage allowances
headings.reviewNote: Directs reimbursement for actual official travel expenses and mileage incurred by juvenile officers in performing duties.

headings.title: Total compensation rule in specified second, third, and fourth class counties
headings.reviewNote: Provides that in second, third, and fourth class counties (except single- or two-county second-class circuits), compensation under this section is the employee's total compensation for juvenile court duties and includes compensation under any other law.

headings.title: Reclassification of class 4 deputy juvenile officers to class 3
headings.reviewNote: Reclassifies all former class 4 deputy juvenile officers to class 3 deputy status effective August 28, 1993.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 editorial headings for 211.381 governing 1985/1986 statutory salary schedules, judicial-department salary adjustments, travel reimbursement, total-compensation rule in certain counties, and class 4 reclassification.

headings.title: Definitions for juvenile officer compensation and retirement systems
headings.reviewNote: Defines county retirement plan, juvenile court employee, juvenile officer, multicounty circuit, single county circuit, and state retirement plan for purposes of this section.

headings.title: Single-county circuit employee status, retirement, and state reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Governs state/county employee and retirement status for single-county circuit juvenile officers and employees before and after July 1, 1999, sets 25% to 50% state reimbursement of 1997 personnel budgets, budget filing, subsection 3 opt-in, and state auditor audits.

headings.title: State employee status and retirement rules for multicounty circuits
headings.reviewNote: Designates multicounty juvenile court personnel as state employees for salary and retirement benefit administration.

headings.title: OSCA verification required for creditable prior service in state plan
headings.reviewNote: Makes receipt of creditable prior service under subsections 2(1)(c) and 3(1)(c) contingent on the office of state courts administrator providing verifiable service dates and monthly salary data to the state retirement plan.

headings.title: Ineligibility for county employees' retirement system fund
headings.reviewNote: Bars any juvenile court employee in any single or multicounty circuit from participating in the county employees' retirement system fund under sections 50.1000 to 50.1200.

headings.title: Maintenance of effort funding obligations of counties
headings.reviewNote: Mandates that counties continue funding local juvenile court budgets through dedicated maintenance of effort payments.

headings.title: Prior service credit for state or MoDOT/highway patrol plan transferees
headings.reviewNote: Grants eligibility for creditable prior service to persons employed on or after July 1, 1999, in positions covered by the state retirement plan or transportation department and highway patrol retirement system who previously served in a non-single-county first-class circuit.

headings.title: Election and county benefit forfeiture for multicounty juvenile officers
headings.reviewNote: Bars multicounty state-employee juvenile officers employed on or after July 1, 1999, from state retirement plan participation unless they elect state benefits on combined county/state salary and forfeit county retirement benefits, triggering an actuarial accrued liability transfer.

headings.title: Retirement election forms provided by state retirement plan
headings.reviewNote: Requires retirement benefit elections to be executed on official forms promulgated by Missouri state retirement system.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 9 editorial headings for 211.393 governing definitions, single-county and multicounty circuit employee/retirement/reimbursement rules, prior service verification, CERF exclusion, maintenance of effort, transferees, multicounty officer elections, and election forms.

headings.title: State contribution not a ceiling on total juvenile officer compensation
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that statutory state salary contributions do not prevent counties from providing additional salary compensation.

headings.title: Exclusion of juvenile state aid funds from Article X state revenue limits
headings.reviewNote: Excludes state funds paid to counties for juvenile administration from total state revenue calculations under Hancock Amendment.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 editorial headings for 211.394 governing county salary supplements above section 211.381 state contribution limits and exclusion from Article X, Section 18 total state revenue.

headings.title: Statutory investigation, reporting, and custodial duties of juvenile officers
headings.reviewNote: Requires juvenile officers to conduct court-ordered investigations, keep written records and offer reports into evidence, take charge of children before and after hearings as ordered, and perform other judge-ordered duties.

headings.title: Peace officer and arrest powers of juvenile officers
headings.reviewNote: Vests juvenile officers with all the authority of sheriffs to make arrests and execute process under the juvenile code.

headings.title: Inter-county cooperation among juvenile officers statewide
headings.reviewNote: Directs juvenile officers of all Missouri counties to cooperate in executing the purposes of the juvenile code.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 editorial headings for 211.401 governing juvenile officer investigative/custodial duties, sheriff arrest powers, and inter-county cooperation.

headings.title: Duty of prosecuting attorneys and city attorneys to assist juvenile officers
headings.reviewNote: Requires prosecutors, circuit attorneys, and county counselors to assist and cooperate with juvenile officers.

headings.title: Duty of law enforcement officers to provide immediate custody information
headings.reviewNote: Requires police officers and sheriffs taking child into custody to notify juvenile court and furnish facts immediately.

headings.title: General duty of public officials and departments to cooperate with court
headings.reviewNote: Mandates that all public departments and officials render jurisdictional assistance to further juvenile code objectives.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 editorial headings for 211.411 governing aid from prosecutors and counselors, immediate law enforcement custody reporting, and cooperation by public officials and organizations.

headings.title: Contempt of court penalty for injuring ward or violating court order
headings.reviewNote: Makes encouraging/aiding conduct injurious to a ward's morals or health or knowingly/negligently disobeying or interfering with a lawful juvenile court order contempt of court, punishable by up to six months in county jail, up to a five-hundred-dollar fine, or both.

headings.title: Mandatory referral to prosecutor for adult child endangerment violations
headings.reviewNote: Requires the juvenile judge to refer information to the prosecuting or circuit attorney when a hearing indicates a person age eighteen or over violated section 568.045 or 568.050 by endangering the welfare of a child.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 editorial headings for 211.421 governing contempt of court penalties for endangering a court ward or violating court orders and mandatory referral of adult endangerment to prosecutors.

headings.title: Juvenile sex offender registration requirements upon felony adjudication
headings.reviewNote: Requires juveniles adjudicated delinquent for felony-equivalent chapter 566 sex offenses (including out-of-state/federal adjudications) to register as juvenile sex offenders, except juveniles age fourteen or older with offenses at least as severe as 18 U.S.C. 2241 who must register as adult offenders under sections 589.400 to 589.425.

headings.title: Ten-day registration, address change notice, and required form contents
headings.reviewNote: Requires supervising agencies, courts, or offenders to register with the county juvenile office within ten days of moving into a county or changing address using a form containing a signed written statement, fingerprints, and photograph.

headings.title: Maintenance and strict confidentiality of juvenile registration forms
headings.reviewNote: Requires juvenile offices to maintain registration forms confidentially with disclosure limited to persons/agencies authorized for juvenile records (including section 211.321), and requires custodial state agencies to notify juvenile offices upon transfer.

headings.title: Disposition and sanctions for failure to register or false reporting
headings.reviewNote: Subjects juveniles who fail to register or give false information to chapter 211 disposition, and makes persons age eighteen or over who commit such violation guilty of a class A misdemeanor under section 211.431.

headings.title: Mandatory registration advisement upon discharge or release from custody
headings.reviewNote: Requires custodial officials upon discharge or release to inform the juvenile of registration duties, obtain the expected address, and report name and address to the juvenile office, excluding temporary release under guard or direct supervision.

headings.title: Termination of juvenile sex offender registration at age twenty-one
headings.reviewNote: Directs that juvenile registration duties terminate at age twenty-one unless adult offender registration is required.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 editorial headings for 211.425 governing juvenile sex offender registration, 10-day registration and form contents, confidentiality and transfer notices, noncompliance penalties, discharge advisement, and termination at age twenty-one.

headings.title: Establishment of county circuit court juvenile justice preservation fund
headings.reviewNote: Creates a juvenile justice preservation fund in each circuit court to implement jurisdiction expansion to eighteen-year-olds.

headings.title: Two-dollar traffic violation surcharge and state fund reversion
headings.reviewNote: Assesses a two-dollar court cost surcharge on county ordinance and state traffic guilty pleas (excluding dismissals and public-paid costs), payable to the county circuit court juvenile justice preservation fund, and reverts state fund balances to the county of origination.

headings.title: Discretionary expenditure of fund by circuit juvenile office
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes expenditures from the county circuit court juvenile justice preservation fund at the circuit juvenile office's discretion solely for implementing and maintaining expansion of juvenile court jurisdiction.

headings.title: Prohibition on expending fund moneys for capital improvements
headings.reviewNote: Bars expenditure of juvenile justice preservation fund moneys for capital construction or physical improvements.

headings.title: Non-supplanting requirement for state and county funding obligations
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits using preservation fund moneys to reduce or replace existing state or county budgetary appropriations.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 editorial headings for 211.435 governing county juvenile justice preservation funds, two-dollar traffic surcharges, discretionary juvenile office spending, capital improvement bar, and non-supplanting rules.

headings.title: General prohibition on courtroom instruments of restraint and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits using handcuffs, chains, or restraints in juvenile court absent finding of imminent flight or physical harm risk.

headings.title: Notice of restraint request to child's attorney prior to hearing
headings.reviewNote: Requires juvenile officer requesting restraints to provide advance notice and specific grounds to child's counsel.

headings.title: Evidentiary hearing and right to be heard before ordering restraints
headings.reviewNote: Mandates judicial hearing providing child's attorney opportunity to contest restraint request before restraints may issue.

headings.title: Hand movement requirements and prohibition on fixed furniture restraints
headings.reviewNote: Requires permitted restraints to allow document handling and strictly forbids fastening child to walls, floors, or furniture.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 editorial headings for 211.436 governing prohibition on courtroom restraints and exceptions, written advance request, evidentiary hearing, and hand-movement/stationary-object rules (Revisor's Note notes H.B. 2637 & 3155 repealed S.B. 888's 2026 version effective 8-28-26, leaving the 2025 S.B. 43 version).

headings.title: Referral of termination information and preliminary inquiry by juvenile officer
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes any person to refer termination information and directs juvenile officer to conduct preliminary investigation.

headings.title: Mandatory termination petition or joinder for foster care, abandonment, or crimes
headings.reviewNote: Requires filing or joining a termination petition (subject to subsection 4) for 15-of-22-month foster care, abandonment of a child under age two (including 60-day neglect under age one or section 210.950 relinquishment), murder/voluntary manslaughter/felony assault of a child, or felony chapter 566, 567, 568, or 573 child-victim convictions.

headings.title: Sixty-day filing deadline after subsection 2 findings without jurisdictional bar
headings.reviewNote: Requires filing or seeking joinder in a termination petition within sixty days of subsection 2 judicial determinations (subject to subsection 4), while stating noncompliance does not deprive the court of jurisdiction.

headings.title: Exceptions to mandatory termination petition filing requirements
headings.reviewNote: Permits withholding termination petition if child is with relatives, compelling reasons exist, or services were not provided.

headings.title: Statutory grounds for termination of parental rights on petition
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes discretionary petitions based on abandonment (age two or older, six months), abuse/neglect (with disability/disease nondiscrimination clause), one-year failure to rectify, conception by forcible or first-degree rape, or parental unfitness (with five statutory presumptions).

headings.title: Judicial determination of child best interests and clear and convincing proof
headings.reviewNote: Requires clear, cogent, and convincing evidence of statutory grounds and an explicit finding that termination serves child's best interests.

headings.title: Mandatory evaluation factors for determining child best interests
headings.reviewNote: Lists statutory factors court must evaluate including emotional ties, parental support payments, and disinterest in child.

headings.title: Weight of infrequent contact and irrelevance of rehabilitation inducement
headings.reviewNote: Permits attaching little or no weight to infrequent visitations, communications, or contributions, and declares irrelevant whether maintaining the parent-child relationship may induce parental rehabilitation.

headings.title: Hearing termination prayers within chapter 453 adoption petitions
headings.reviewNote: Permits the court in chapter 453 adoption actions to hear and determine a prayer for termination of parental rights with the same effect as a petition under subsection 2, 4, or 5.

headings.title: Parental disability or disease not basis for action without causal harm
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits using a parent's disability or disease as a basis for a need-of-care determination, custody removal, or termination of parental rights without a specific showing of a causal relation to harm to the child.

headings.title: Termination of biological father's rights for conception by forcible or first-degree rape
headings.reviewNote: Permits the victim mother (or someone on a minor mother's behalf) to petition to terminate the biological father's rights upon clear, cogent, and convincing proof of forcible or first-degree rape and resulting conception, plus preponderance proof of child's best interests.

headings.title: Financial support, inheritance, and public assistance protections in rape cases
headings.reviewNote: Permits ordering pregnancy/child expenses, child support, inheritance rights (barring father/kindred inheritance), or beneficiary designations with the mother's informed consent without granting father parental rights, and bars requiring support pursuit for public assistance under 42 U.S.C. 654(29).

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 12 editorial headings for 211.447 governing preliminary inquiries, mandatory and discretionary termination grounds, 60-day filing deadline, exceptions, clear-and-convincing standard, evaluation factors, adoption prayers, parental disability bar, and rape-conception terminations and financial benefits.

headings.title: Required contents and factual allegations in termination petition
headings.reviewNote: Specifies mandatory allegations including child identity, parental domicile, grounds, and custody status in termination petition.

headings.title: Joinder of termination cases for multiple children in same family
headings.reviewNote: Permits the court to join termination of parental rights cases for more than one child in the same family for disposition in one proceeding if joinder is in the best interests of each child.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 editorial headings for 211.452 governing termination petition venue and required contents, and joinder of termination cases for multiple children in the same family.

headings.title: Manner of service of summons under sections 506.150 and 506.160
headings.reviewNote: Requires service of summons as in civil cases under section 506.150, or by mail or publication under section 506.160 if service cannot be made under section 506.150 and is not waived.

headings.title: Persons required to be summoned and receive copy of petition
headings.reviewNote: Lists persons who must be summoned and receive the petition: parents (including putative father affirmatively asserting paternity, unless consent filed), guardian, custodian, foster parent/relative/placement provider, and others deemed necessary.

headings.title: Statutory text excusing service for unknown or unlocatable parent
headings.reviewNote: States the court shall not require service for a parent whose identity is unknown and unascertainable or who cannot be located; archived 1988 source annotation cites In Interest of Loveheart, 762 S.W.2d 32 (Mo. banc), holding this unconstitutional insofar as it removes notice by publication.

headings.title: Waiver of appearance or service of summons by required recipient
headings.reviewNote: Permits any person required to receive summons to waive appearance or service of summons.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 editorial headings for 211.453 governing manner of service, persons required to be summoned, unknown-parent service text (with archived 1988 constitutional annotation), and waiver of appearance or service.

headings.title: Thirty-day meeting with court to verify service and request study
headings.reviewNote: Requires the juvenile officer within thirty days after petition filing to meet with the court to determine that all parties have been served and request an investigation and social study.

headings.title: Discretionary extension of time for completing service of summons
headings.reviewNote: Permits the court to extend the time for service if all required parties have not been served and the court finds service may be forthcoming and serves the child's best interests.

headings.title: Investigation, social study report, and fifteen-day pre-hearing access
headings.reviewNote: Requires an investigation and social study (except in section 211.444 cases) with a written report on parental fitness and child condition, and mandates making all ordered evaluations and reports available to parties, attorneys, guardians ad litem, and volunteer advocates at least fifteen days before any dispositional hearing.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 editorial headings for 211.455 governing 30-day service determination meeting, discretionary service extensions, and mandatory investigation/social study with 15-day pre-hearing access.

headings.title: Dispositional hearing within thirty days, subpoenas, and division testimony
headings.reviewNote: Requires holding the dispositional hearing within thirty days after the section 211.455 meeting, grants subpoena and evidence rights, permits compelling investigating division personnel to testify without privilege subject to cross-examination, and provides civil witness fees and mileage.

headings.title: Stenographic recording of dispositional termination proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Requires stenographic recording of testimony and proceedings in all parental rights termination hearings.

headings.title: Civil immunity for mandatory child abuse reporters participating in hearings
headings.reviewNote: Grants statutory immunity from civil liability to persons reporting abuse or participating in good faith in proceedings.

headings.title: Abrogation of privileged communications except clergy and legal counsel
headings.reviewNote: Abrogates professional privileges in termination hearings except for attorney-client and priest-penitent communications.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 editorial headings for 211.459 governing dispositional hearing timing and testimony, stenographic recording, good-faith reporter immunity, and abrogation of non-clergy/non-attorney privileges.

headings.title: Mandatory appointment of guardian ad litem or child's counsel
headings.reviewNote: Requires immediate appointment of a guardian ad litem or legal counsel for the child in all parental termination cases.

headings.title: Right to counsel and appointed attorney for indigent parents
headings.reviewNote: Requires notice in the summons of the parent's or guardian's right to counsel, mandates appointing counsel upon request and financial inability, and requires appointing a guardian ad litem for a minor or incompetent parent.

headings.title: Duties of guardian ad litem or child's counsel across all stages
headings.reviewNote: Requires the guardian ad litem or child's counsel to serve as legal representative with examination/subpoena/appeal authority, advocate for the child and conduct interviews, and protect the rights and welfare of a minor or incompetent parent.

headings.title: Payment of court costs by county or custodial agency or person
headings.reviewNote: Requires court costs to be paid by the county where the proceeding is instituted, except that the court may require the agency or person having or receiving legal or actual custody to pay the costs.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 editorial headings for 211.462 governing appointment of guardian ad litem or child's counsel, parent counsel and minor/incompetent parent GAL, advocacy duties, and court cost allocation.

headings.title: Right of prospective adoptive foster parents to present evidence
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes foster parents and relatives seeking permanent adoption to present evidence at dispositional termination hearings.

headings.title: Right of non-adoptive foster custodians to testify at hearings
headings.reviewNote: Guarantees current foster parents and legal custodians not seeking adoption notice and opportunity to testify at hearings.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 editorial headings for 211.464 governing presentation of evidence by prospective adoptive foster parents or relatives and notice/testimony rights for non-adoptive foster custodians.

headings.title: Order terminating parental rights and transferring legal custody
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes court order terminating parental rights and awarding legal custody to children's division or approved agency.

headings.title: Termination of rights of single consenting or offending parent
headings.reviewNote: Permits terminating rights of only one parent where grounds exist or consent is given, preserving rights of other parent.

headings.title: Termination order permitted regardless of immediate adoptive availability
headings.reviewNote: Affirms court authority to terminate parental rights whether or not child is currently placed in an adoptive home.

headings.title: Discretionary alternatives when termination is not in child's best interests
headings.reviewNote: Permits the court, when grounds exist but termination is not in the child's best interests (including a child age fourteen or older objecting), to dismiss and return custody, retain jurisdiction with custody and six-month mandatory review, or appoint a chapter 475 guardian.

headings.title: Required jurisdictional findings and statutory grounds in termination order
headings.reviewNote: Mandates that termination order recite specific jurisdictional facts, statutory grounds, and best interest findings.

headings.title: Final judgment status of termination orders for appellate review
headings.reviewNote: Designates granting or denial of a parental rights termination petition as a final appealable judgment.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 editorial headings for 211.477 governing termination orders and custody transfers, single-parent termination, adoptive availability irrelevance, alternatives when termination is not in best interests, required recitals, and final judgment status.

headings.title: Applicability to proceedings commenced on or after September 28, 1985
headings.reviewNote: Applies sections 211.442 to 211.487 to all proceedings commenced on or after September 28, 1985.

headings.title: Governing law for termination proceedings pending prior to September 28, 1985
headings.reviewNote: Provides that termination petitions pending prior to September 28, 1985, are governed by the law in effect at filing.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 editorial headings for 211.487 governing applicability of sections 211.442 to 211.487 on or after September 28, 1985, and governing law for pending actions.

headings.title: Multi-county agreements to establish regional juvenile detention district
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes any two or more counties to enter agreements establishing a regional juvenile detention district.

headings.title: County commission ordinances or resolutions approving regional agreements
headings.reviewNote: Requires the county commission of each county desiring to join to approve an ordinance or resolution to join and approve the agreement specifying each county's duties.

headings.title: Re-execution of agreement upon admission of new member county
headings.reviewNote: Requires regional detention agreement to be amended and reapproved by all member counties when a new county joins.

headings.title: Mandatory provisions and operational cost formulas in regional agreements
headings.reviewNote: Specifies essential agreement terms including district name, participating counties, and operational cost formulas.

headings.title: Municipal and county contracts with regional detention center commission
headings.reviewNote: Permits any county, city, town, or village to contract with a regional juvenile detention center commission for holding its juvenile offenders.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 editorial headings for 211.500 governing multi-county regional juvenile detention district agreements, county approvals, admitting new members, mandatory agreement terms, and local contracts.

headings.title: State courts administrator duty to collect juvenile certification data
headings.reviewNote: Directs office of state courts administrator to collect comprehensive data on juvenile certification filings and dispositions.

headings.title: Required data categories on certification petitions and outcomes
headings.reviewNote: Requires collected data to include annual certification petition filings, dispositions, offenses, race of juveniles, and the number of juveniles who waived their right to counsel.

headings.title: Annual public dissemination of juvenile certification statistics
headings.reviewNote: Mandates that collected juvenile certification data and statistical reports be made publicly available annually.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 editorial headings for 211.600 governing OSCA collection of juvenile certification petition data, five required annual data categories, and annual public availability.
